principles: Evaluate on the adopter's real product or a representative public fixture rather than on marketing claims.
Start reporting-only; enforcement is a separate decision after findings and false positives are reviewed.
Keep source in the adopter environment; the source audit requires no network service and executes no audited project code.
Measure incremental value beside existing accessibility, localization, browser, and security tooling rather than claiming to replace it.
Record both useful findings and false positives so adoption decisions are evidence-led.
Keep standards references narrower than certification claims.

profiles.title: Arabic/RTL source assurance in CI
inputs: A representative web repository or selected source directories.
Optional existing accessibility/lint results for comparison.
A reviewer who can classify whether physical layout choices are intentional.
outputs: Structured JSON findings with rule, severity, location, remediation, and standard rationale.
SARIF 2.1.0 suitable for existing code-scanning workflows.
Optional counted SHA-256 baseline for reviewed historical debt.
A candidate repository policy defining rule severity and enforcement threshold.

metrics.description: Findings accepted by the adopter as real defects or engineering risks that were not already blocked by its current pipeline.
metrics.evidence: Reviewed finding disposition table grouped by Rawafid rule ID.
metrics.target: At least one materially useful unique finding or a defensible zero-findings result on a demonstrably clean scope.

metrics.description: Share of reviewed findings classified as not applicable or intentionally physical after technical review.
metrics.evidence: Disposition counts with reasons; do not infer correctness from unreviewed findings.
metrics.target: Low enough for the adopter's intended severity threshold; advisory rules may remain non-blocking.

metrics.description: Ability to baseline reviewed legacy occurrences while leaving an additional matching defect active.
metrics.evidence: Before/after CI run using a committed baseline and a deliberately introduced duplicate fixture.
metrics.target: Historical occurrences suppressed; additional occurrence remains active.

decisionGate: Adopt reporting-only if the results add review value with acceptable noise.
Adopt warning/error enforcement only after the rule policy and baseline are code-reviewed.
Do not adopt a blocking gate when the evaluated scope is not representative of the product.
nonClaims: Passing the source audit is not WCAG, ISO/IEC 40500, EN 301 549, EAA, or Unicode-security certification.

profiles.title: RTL design-system interoperability
inputs: A representative set of navigation, form, menu, dialog, tabs, grid/table, pagination, and mixed-direction components.
LTR and RTL locales or deterministic fixtures.
Keyboard interaction requirements and supported browser targets.
outputs: Keyboard/focus results for direction-aware composite interactions.
axe-core regression evidence on controlled fixtures.
Logical-edge and narrow-viewport invariants suitable for visual regression integration.

metrics.description: Required RTL interaction invariants that behave consistently across supported browser projects.
metrics.evidence: Playwright results for Chromium, Firefox, WebKit, and mobile Chromium or adopter-equivalent browser matrix.
metrics.target: No unexplained direction-specific failure in the evaluated critical component set.

metrics.description: Direction-aware keyboard behavior remains coherent without changing semantic source order merely for visual mirroring.
metrics.evidence: Recorded arrow/Home/End/tab/focus assertions for evaluated composites.
metrics.target: Reviewed interaction contract passes in both LTR and RTL for critical components.

metrics.description: Paired LTR/RTL fixtures expose stable logical-edge and overflow invariants that the adopter can connect to its visual toolchain.
metrics.evidence: Deterministic fixture URLs/results and any adopter-owned screenshot diff.
metrics.target: At least one reusable paired fixture for each critical component family selected for the pilot.

decisionGate: Adopt primitives/tests that remove repeated RTL-specific integration code or expose regressions not covered by the current system.
Keep framework lifecycle behavior in adopter/framework adapters rather than widening the core without evidence.
Do not equate an axe-clean fixture with complete assistive-technology conformance.
nonClaims: The browser suite does not prove usability with every assistive technology or linguistic correctness for every Arabic locale.

profiles.title: Arabic localization and locale-boundary QA
inputs: A representative source/target message catalog or public fixture.
Target locales and explicit script requirements where applicable.
Formatting/input requirements for numbers, dates, pluralization, and mixed-script labels.
outputs: Catalog parity and structural QA evidence.
Bidi-control/isolate and contextual zero-width findings where applicable.
Localized number/formatting interoperability evidence using host Intl behavior.

metrics.description: Placeholder, key, markup-token, or bidi-structure defects identified before human linguistic review or release.
metrics.evidence: Machine-readable localization QA result plus reviewer disposition.
metrics.target: Structural defects are reproducible and can be blocked without judging linguistic style.

metrics.description: Explicit script requirements are not silently discarded by locale fallback.
metrics.evidence: Locale fallback/property tests using adopter-relevant BCP 47 tags.
metrics.target: No silent cross-script fallback in the evaluated explicit-script cases.

metrics.description: Required localized numeric forms can be formatted and parsed under the declared runtime contract without destructive punctuation normalization.
metrics.evidence: Roundtrip fixtures for adopter-selected locales/numbering systems.
metrics.target: All agreed representative valid inputs roundtrip; invalid grouping remains rejectable.

decisionGate: Integrate machine checks when they catch structural/localization-engineering defects without replacing translator review.
Document ICU/CLDR/runtime-dependent behavior rather than freezing unstable locale details into a false universal contract.
Do not claim native-language quality from machine validation alone.
nonClaims: Localization QA verifies documented structural and runtime invariants, not translation quality or cultural appropriateness by itself.

profiles.title: Unicode bidi and display-risk review
inputs: Representative untrusted labels, identifiers, usernames, filenames, messages, or generated display strings.
The product context defining which mixed-script and zero-width behavior is legitimate.
Existing source-security or identifier policies for comparison.
outputs: Display-risk diagnostics for bidi controls/overrides, unbalanced isolates, zero-width characters, and represented scripts.
Source-level bidi findings suitable for code review/code scanning.
A documented boundary between display-risk signals and full confusable/source-security analysis.

metrics.description: Selected suspicious strings produce stable, explainable diagnostics without destructive source normalization.
metrics.evidence: Versioned corpus and expected diagnostic results.
metrics.target: All agreed pilot vectors reproduce deterministically under the declared runtime.

metrics.description: The adopter can distinguish legitimate multilingual/mixed-script content from contexts that require stronger restrictions.
metrics.evidence: Reviewed context-specific policy notes tied to diagnostic classes.
metrics.target: No generic rule is represented as universally unsafe when product context is required.

decisionGate: Use Rawafid signals as defense-in-depth where they add display/bidi context to existing security controls.
Escalate to a dedicated Unicode security policy/data implementation when confusable restriction levels or identifier security profiles are required.
Do not market the current diagnostics as a complete UTS #39 or Trojan Source analyzer.
nonClaims: Rawafid display-risk diagnostics are deliberately narrower than complete Unicode confusable, identifier-profile, or source-code security analysis.
